{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Cuisine of Italy]] | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]]

{{decameron}}

==Ingredients==  
*3 [[Cookbook:Turnip|turnips]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
*[[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] gravy
*8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] crushed [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
*4 cups [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]], [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], or vegetable [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]], brought to a boil
*⅓ cup white [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]], washed

==Procedure==
#Arrange the turnip slices on a rack over a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]]. Sprinkle with salt, cover them with a dish, and let them stand for about 2 hours until the water has run out of them.  
#Put the slices in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]], and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] them slightly in butter until softened.  
#Add the gravy and tomatoes. Cook for a few minutes, then pour it into the [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiling]] stock.  
#Boil for 30 minutes. Serve hot.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Minestra loses its flavour if it is boiled too long. In Lombardy, however, rice, macaroni, etc., are rarely boiled enough for English tastes.
